rationale: The workflow already applies dependency caching (Swatinem/rust-cache@v2) to all Rust jobs (api-check, api-test, api-document, cli-check), satisfying the P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern's method of caching dependency download state while keeping required checks. The only measured evidence (experiment:batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200) supports adding actions/cache@v4 for Gradle dependencies (~/.gradle/caches), which is a different build system and does not transfer to this Rust/Cargo repository. The pattern's contraindication 'An equivalent cache already exists' applies to the Rust jobs. The common-check and common-test jobs run make targets with no evidence that they fetch cacheable dependencies or that a cache key/inputs (lockfile, environment) are identifiable. No other pattern's preconditions are met: there is no matrix (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST), no schedules (P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE, P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE), no Bazel (P-LIT-BAZEL-*), no history-derived timeout data (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT, P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT), no change-dependency data for test/build selection (P-LIT-SELECT, P-LIT-BUILD-SELECT, P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER), and no identified unused outputs (P-LIT-UNUSED-OUTPUTS).
